title: How do we construct the perpendicular bisector of X Y?
description: A segment X Y is given, and only a ruler and a compass are allowed. Equal arcs above and below meet at two points, and the line through them is the perpendicular bisector. Keeko's doubt, that a smaller opening is neater, is tested and the arcs are shown not to meet.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal arcs from both ends, with the opening more than half of X Y, give two points, and the line through them is the perpendicular bisector. Watch for students who pick an opening smaller than half the segment.

source: Draw a line segment XY. Construct its perpendicular bisector
video_script.why: The child has seen why equal arcs give points on the perpendicular bisector, but has not yet followed every move of the construction on paper.
video_script.substitution: Equal arcs from both ends, with an opening of more than half of X Y, meet at two points, and the ruler joins them.
video_script.anchor: A line segment X Y: construct its perpendicular bisector with an unmarked ruler and a compass, and mark the midpoint.
video_script.wrong_answer: a radius smaller than half of X Y
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko opens the compass to less than half of X Y, so the arc from X and the arc from Y stop short of each other and never meet.
video_script.payoff_line: The line through the two meeting points is the perpendicular bisector

final_answer.value: AB, the line through the two meeting points of equal arcs, is the perpendicular bisector of XY; it meets XY at its midpoint O
final_answer.spoken: the line through the two meeting points is the perpendicular bisector, and it meets X Y at its midpoint O

hold_back: the line through the two meeting points
never_show: the finished line AB before step four
maths_rules: Opening r with r more than half of XY, so that arcs from X and from Y meet.
Arcs of radius r from X and Y above XY meet at A; arcs of the same radius r below XY meet at B; AX = AY = BX = BY = r.
Line AB meets XY at O; triangle ABX is congruent to triangle ABY by SSS, and triangle AOX is congruent to triangle AOY by SAS, so OX = OY and angle AOX = angle AOY = 90 degrees.
Slip: with the opening less than half of XY, the arcs from X and Y stop short of each other and do not meet, so no point A exists.
video_script.design: One idea: equal arcs above and below give two points, and the ruler joins them. The segment X Y stays the whole video. Keeko's doubt is a smaller opening.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A line that cuts a segment in half at a right angle is called a perpendicular bisector.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We draw it with arcs. The compass must open to more than half the length of X Y.
